title: Count Vowel Substrings of a String
statement: Call a non-empty contiguous piece of `word` a *vowel substring* when every character in it is one of `a`, `e`, `i`, `o`, `u` and each of those five letters appears in it at least once. Return how many vowel substrings `word` has; substrings at different positions are counted separately even if their text is the same.
constraints: word contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

With at most 100 characters there are only about 5,000 substrings, so we can simply enumerate them. Two observations keep it tidy: once a substring hits a consonant, every longer substring from the same start contains it too, so we stop extending; and a set of the vowels seen so far tells us in O(1) whether all five are present. A pure brute force that slices every substring and re-scans it is O(n³) but still fine here; the set version avoids the re-scan.

## Approach

1. Put the five vowels in a set `vowels` and set `count` to 0.
2. For each `start`, begin an empty set `seen`.
3. Extend `end` from `start` to the right. Stop at the first character that is not a vowel.
4. Add `word[end]` to `seen`. If `seen` now holds all five vowels, the substring `word[start..end]` qualifies, so increase `count`.
5. Return `count`.

## Example 1, step by step

`word = "aeiouu"`. From `start = 0`, `seen` grows to `{a, e, i, o}` by `end = 3`; at `end = 4` it reaches size 5 and `count = 1`, and at `end = 5` (another `u`) it is still size 5, so `count = 2`. Every later start has lost the `a`, so `seen` never reaches 5. The answer is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n²): each start extends at most to the end of the string, with O(1) set work per step.
- Space: O(1): `seen` holds at most five letters.

## Pitfalls

- Do not keep extending past a consonant; a substring containing one never counts.
- Keep counting after the fifth vowel appears: every longer all-vowel extension also qualifies.
- Count substrings by position, not by distinct text.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `vowels` | the set `{a, e, i, o, u}` |
| `count` | vowel substrings found so far |
| `start`, `end` | first and last index of the current substring |
| `seen` | distinct vowels in `word[start..end]` |

narration.8: A consonant ruins this and every longer substring from this start, so stop.
